full_judgment:
12. The defendant No. 1, the Trustee of the Port of Chittagong in their witness statements contended that the suit is not maintainable, that the alleged notice under Section 109 of the Chittagong Port Act is not a proper and valid notice, the suit is barred by limitation and that there is no cause of action against this defendant. The defendant No. I denied any liability for the alleged loss for the non-delivery of the said consignment. The entire port area and the cargo were under absolute control of the occupation forces and non-local and under the abnormal condition and circumstances prevailing beyond the control of the port administration at that time. During the war of liberation many cars, jeeps, trucks and buses etc. and other imported consignments had been missing from the port area. It is common knowledge that the Pak army and the allied miscreants took away many of those vehicles to Karachi and other unknown destinations and all efforts to locate such vehicles hardly met with success. The car obviously was the victim of the circumstances and the plaintiff was informed accordingly. The defendant asserted that there was no negligence or carelessness on the part of the staff of this defendant and no loss occurred for any fault on the part of the present port administration. 

 2. Is the suit barred by limitation? 

 15. Mr. Moqbul Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for Mr. Muzammel Huq, the learned Advocate for the appellant argues that the learned trial court should have found that the notice under section 109 of the Chittagong Port Act is not proper notice and that the suit is barred by limitation. No further argues that in view of Section 50, Sub-section 2, the claim of the plaintiff is not maintainable, that the trial court failed to note that the delivery of the car was not taken within 5 days of the landing of the consignment and as such the defendant No. 1 was not at all liable. He has further argued that the trial court having failed to note that the port was during the disturbed period under the occupation of the Pak army and as such the alleged loss has not been caused due to the negligence of the port employees. 

 22. Now as regards the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the suit is barred by limitation Mr. Makbul Ahmed during his argument could not show or point out anything from the notice that the notice was not served or that notice was not a proper notice as contemplated under Section 109 of the Chittagong Port Act. The learned Advocate strenuously argued that the plaintiff knew about the arrival of the Cargo and the discharge of the Cargo with the defendant No. 1 and that the plaintiff had definite know-ledge of the loss of the car from defendant No. 3 on 25.5.71 and that therefore from that date this suit is barred by limitation. 

 23. Mr. M.A. Jalil the learned Advocate for the plaintiff respondent submits that in view of the facts and circumstances of the case the suit is not barred by limitation. In this connect the learned Advocate cited before us the case of Chittagong Port Authority Vs. Md. Ishaque and others reported in 35 DLR (AD) 364 in support of his contention. 

 24. It appears from ext. 5(q), a letter dated 25.5.71 written by the defendant No. 3 to the plaintiff wherein the plaintiff was in-formed that on enquiry from the clearing agent the defendant No. 3 has been informed that the suit car is not traceable in the port and that it might have been taken away by the defence service people. This letter gives preliminary information that clearing agent on completing formalities could not locate the suit car. But from Ext. A(2), a letter dated 6.7.71 written by the plaintiff to the Chairman of the Port of Trust of the Port of Chittagong. It appears that the plaintiff intimated to him that the plaintiff has been informed that his imported car reached the port in perfectly good condition but soon after conclusion of formalities by Custom Clearance they found that the suit car is not available in the Jetty for clearing. Thereafter on receipt of the notice dated 24.3.71 under Section 109 of the Chittagong Port. Act by the plaintiff to the defendant No. 1, the Port authority by its letter Ext. A(3) dated 17.7.7)119.7.11 informed the plaintiff that it has come to light that many trucks, buses etc. have been missing from the Port and suit car also appears to be the victim of such circumstances. Investigation was said to be gill in progress regarding the missing of things from the part which is a protected Area. On completion of investigation reference was likely to follow. Thereafter as per letter or Ext. A(4) dated 26.9.72 written by defendant No. 1 to the plaintiff, the plaintiff was informed that Pak Army and other miscreants took away the vehicles from the part. The car in question was said to be the victim of such circumstances. From Ext. A(3) it appears that the defendant No. 1 did not deny his liability but tried to give an indication to the plaintiff that they were investigating to locate the suit car and ultimately by Ext. A (4) dated 26.9.72 they have tried to say the finality of their effort, The plaintiff filed 'the suit showing the cause of action considering this letter as the date of repudiation of the liability of defendant No. 1 as a Bailee. So on consideration of these materials read with the evidence of D.W. 1 we are of the view that the plaintiff gave the notice in time and the suit is not barred by limitation. In this regard Subsection (2) of section 109 may be quoted which runs as follows:— 

 25. Sub-section (1) of section 109 of the said Act provides for a notice in writing to give jurisdiction to the court to try the suit and unless that notice is proved the court shall dismiss the suit. He will not proceed with the trial of the suit, but Subsection (2) deals with the period of limitation. 

 26. From a reading of this sub-section (2) of section 109 of the said Act it appears that the suit shall be commenced within six months next after the accrual of right to sue and not afterwards. In the case of the Chittagong Port Authority Vs. Sadharan Bima Corporation reported in B.C.R. 82 (SD) page 4 it has been observed that the expression accrual of the right to sue as used in Section 109 (2) of the Chittagong Port Act means the accrual of cause of action and that the plaintiff will be entitled to add the notice period under sub-section (1) of section 109 of the Chittagong Port Act to the period of limitation prescribed under sub-section (2) of the said Section 109. So we are inclined to hold that in the present case the right to sue accrues from the actual date of knowledge of the loss of the car. In this particular case the right to sue accused as soon as the defendant No. 1 who informed the plaintiff that their last attempt has failed on 26,9.72 vide Ext. A(4). Therefore we do not find any substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant so far as the question of bar of limitation under section 109 atilt Chittagong Port Act is concerned.
